text: Playbooks are the platform's scheduled automations. Each playbook bundles a sequence of steps and fires on a cron schedule defined in its trigger block; the scheduler evaluates due playbooks every minute and enqueues a run for each one whose cron expression matches.

A playbook run executes its steps in order. Steps can call platform actions, wait on approvals, or branch on a prior step's output. Pausing a playbook keeps its definition but suspends the schedule until it is resumed from the Command Center.

Editing a playbook's cron expression takes effect on the next scheduler tick. Common schedules: nightly at 02:00 UTC for maintenance playbooks, every Monday 08:00 for weekly report playbooks. Run history for each playbook is kept for 90 days.

Task assignment is skill-based. When a task lands on the board, the dispatcher scores every active agent against the task's required skills and claims it for the highest-scoring agent that has spare capacity; ties break toward the agent with the emptiest queue.

Agents advertise skills in their blueprint. Routing overrides exist: a task tagged with an explicit agent id skips scoring entirely, and a team-scoped task only considers agents on that team. Unclaimed tasks re-enter the dispatch sweep every five minutes.

When a run fails partway, the engine marks the failing step, keeps completed steps' outputs, and applies the retry policy: up to three retries with exponential backoff starting at 30 seconds. A step that exhausts retries moves the run to failed and fires the failure notification.

Failed runs can be resumed from the failing step rather than restarted — the resume keeps earlier step outputs. Repeated failures on the same schedule trip the circuit breaker, which pauses the automation until a manual run succeeds.

Billing runs monthly on the first. Each workspace is charged for its plan tier plus metered usage (agent-hours and storage) from the previous month; the invoice line items show plan, usage, and any credits applied.

Invoices are emailed to the billing contact and available under Settings → Billing. Payment is collected by card on file three days after invoice issue; failed payment retries twice before the account is flagged past-due.

Single sign-on uses SAML 2.0. To enable it, an admin uploads the identity provider metadata XML under Settings → Security, maps email as the NameID, and assigns the default role for just-in-time provisioned users.
After SSO is enforced, password logins are disabled for everyone except break-glass admins. Okta and Azure AD are the tested identity providers; group claims can map to workspace teams.

API requests authenticate with a bearer key created under Settings → API Keys. Keys are scoped per workspace and per capability; server-to-server integrations should use a service key, never a personal one.
Rotate API keys by creating the replacement first, cutting traffic over, then revoking the old key. Revocation is immediate. Keys unused for 180 days are flagged for review in the security digest.

Deploys promote through staging. Merging to the release branch auto-deploys staging; after the smoke checklist passes, an engineer promotes the same build to production from the deploy dashboard — production never builds from scratch.

The staging checklist: migrations applied cleanly, health endpoint green, one end-to-end playbook run, error rate flat for 15 minutes. Rollback is redeploying the previous build id from the same dashboard.
Incident response: severity 1 means customer-facing outage — page the on-call engineer immediately and open the incident channel; the incident commander posts updates every 30 minutes until resolved.
Severity 2 covers degraded service with a workaround, handled in business hours. Every severity 1 incident gets a post-mortem within five working days, blameless, with actions tracked on the board.
Customer data is retained for the life of the subscription plus 60 days. On workspace deletion, documents, chunks, and vectors are purged within 24 hours; backups age out after 35 days.

Data-deletion requests under GDPR are honoured within 30 days and cover derived stores too: memory entries, embeddings, and analytics rollups keyed to the subject. Deletion is verified by the compliance sweep.

New workspace onboarding checklist: create the workspace, invite the first admin, connect at least one integration, upload the starter knowledge documents, and run the welcome playbook to verify the pipeline end to end.
A workspace is considered activated once an agent has completed three real tasks. The onboarding dashboard tracks each step; stalled workspaces get a check-in email after seven days.
The analytics dashboard shows usage charts per workspace: task throughput, agent utilisation, and token spend, each over a selectable window. Hover any point for the daily breakdown.
Every chart exports: use the kebab menu → Export CSV for the raw series, or schedule a weekly email digest. Export respects the viewer's team scope.
Access control is role-based. Owners manage billing and security, admins manage members and settings, members use the product, and viewers are read-only. Roles apply per workspace.

Team scoping restricts documents: a document assigned to teams is visible only to members of those teams; documents with no team are workspace-public. Agents inherit the team scope of their blueprint.
Q2 release notes: the board gained swim-lanes, deliverable templates support brand kits, and the mobile app shipped read-only mission views. Forty-one bugs closed.
Growth review notes: trial-to-paid conversion held at 22%, the onboarding rework is the top lever, and marketing wants case studies from the two logistics customers next quarter.
Winter line catalogue. The Aurora parka is the flagship: SKU MT-4417-BLK (black), MT-4417-NVY (navy), MT-4417-FRN (fern), sizes XS through 3XL. Fill weight 700, recycled shell.
The Aurora parka is the best-selling winter jacket three seasons running; black outsells navy two to one. Companion pieces: the Ridge fleece MT-3102 and the Summit beanie MT-1201.
Catalogue data hygiene: every SKU carries colourway suffix (-BLK, -NVY, -FRN), a size curve, and a season tag. New winter items must be tagged W26 before they appear in storefront filters.
Returns: customers have 30 days from delivery to request a return from their order page. Items must be unworn with tags. The prepaid label is generated automatically for domestic orders.
Refunds are issued to the original payment method within five working days of the warehouse scanning the return in. Exchanges ship as soon as the inbound label is scanned, not when it arrives.

Shipping zones: zone 1 (UK mainland) ships DPD next-day; zone 2 (EU) ships DHL road, 3-5 days; zone 3 (North America) ships FedEx cross-border, 5-8 days. Highlands and islands carry a one-day surcharge.
Carrier selection is automatic by zone and weight; orders over 20kg upgrade to pallet freight. Peak-season cutoffs move a day earlier from mid-November.

Inventory sync error codes: ERR-SYNC-409 means the warehouse system rejected a stock update because the item version was stale — re-pull the item and replay. ERR-SYNC-404 means the SKU is unknown downstream; check the catalogue push.
ERR-SYNC-503 is the warehouse API circuit breaker — sync retries automatically every 15 minutes. Stock counts failing to update usually trace to 409 conflicts on fast-moving SKUs during flash sales.
Northwind supply agreement: payment terms are net-45 from goods-received, delivery within 21 days of purchase order, and a 2% early-payment discount inside 14 days.

Northwind quality clause: defect rate above 1.5% in any received batch triggers a full-batch inspection at supplier cost. The agreement renews annually each April unless notice is given 60 days prior.
Promo calendar: the winter sale opens the last Friday of November and runs 10 days; a mid-January clearance follows for end-of-line stock. Sitewide discounts never stack with voucher codes.
Discount rules: seasonal reductions apply automatically at basket level by season tag; clearance items are capped at 60% off; staff discount is 30% and excludes gift cards.

Warehouse picking: orders batch into pick waves every 30 minutes. A picker follows the scanner's route through the aisles, scanning each bin and item; short picks flag the order for stock investigation.
After picking, orders move to the pack bench: weight check against expected mass catches wrong-item errors before the label prints. Packed orders sort by carrier collection time.
Card payments run through Stripe. The storefront tokenises the card client-side; the order service captures on dispatch, not at checkout, so cancelled orders never need a refund.
Stripe gateway webhooks: payment_intent.succeeded confirms capture, charge.dispute.created opens a dispute case automatically. Webhook signing secrets rotate quarterly.
Customer-service escalation matrix: tier 1 handles order status and returns; anything involving refunds over £200, legal threats, or press goes to tier 2 within one hour.
Tier 2 owns goodwill gestures up to £75 without approval. If a customer remains unhappy after tier 2, the duty manager takes the case and responds the same day.
Contoso supply agreement: payment terms are net-30 from invoice, delivery within 30 days of purchase order, no early-payment discount. Contoso supplies accessories only.
Contoso minimums: order quantities start at 500 units per SKU with a 5% tolerance on delivered quantity. The agreement is reviewed every two years.
Product photography: shoot on the neutral grey set, 3:4 crop, minimum 2400px on the long edge; one on-model and one flat-lay per colourway before a listing goes live.
Stocktake: a rolling count covers every bin location once per quarter; the year-end full count is the last Sunday of January with the warehouse closed to dispatch.
Stocktake variance threshold: differences above 2% of bin value or £150 (whichever is lower) trigger a recount and an investigation note before adjustments post to the ledger.
